title: Electric Service Agreement Closed-Agreement Balance and Transfer Amount: Billing Operations Method Statement
content:
## Method

This statement sets out how Billing Operations works the balance of a closed **Electric Service Agreement** and the transfer amount that is debited to the customer's receiving agreement when that balance is transferred.

**1. Closed-agreement balance.** The closed agreement's balance is the sum of its bills and charges less the sum of its payments and credits. Every bill, charge, payment and credit recorded on the closed agreement enters, whatever its date; no look-back period limits the sum.

**2. Transfer amount.** The transfer amount is that balance, rounded to the cent. Rounding to the cent is the last operation on the transfer amount and happens once, on the finished figure.

**3. Final bill's unpaid portion.** The final bill's unpaid portion is the smaller of the final bill's amount and the closed agreement's balance, never below zero. It is read from the closed agreement's final bill (the bill issued as its final bill) and the balance worked under item 1.

The closed agreement's schedule supplies every rate, fee and period used for the closed agreement.

## Worked figures (hypothetical inputs)

| Hypothetical record on the closed agreement | USD |
|---|---|
| Regular bills issued | 312.40 |
| Final bill | 118.40 |
| Charges posted | 6.35 |
| Payments posted | 250.00 |
| Credits posted | 12.00 |

- Bills and charges: 312.40 plus 118.40 plus 6.35 gives 437.15.
- Payments and credits: 250.00 plus 12.00 gives 262.00.
- Balance: 437.15 less 262.00 gives 175.15.
- Transfer amount: 175.15, rounded to the cent, is USD 175.15.
- Final bill's unpaid portion: the smaller of 118.40 and 175.15 is USD 118.40.

A second hypothetical closed agreement whose balance is USD 64.20 and whose final bill was USD 118.40 has a final bill's unpaid portion of USD 64.20, because the balance is the smaller figure.

## Points of judgement

- **Which payments count?** All payments posted to the closed agreement, at any date, are subtracted with its credits.
- **Is the balance rounded before the transfer amount is finished?** No; the single rounding to the cent is applied to the transfer amount itself.
